name: Denise Ho
life: “I still remember watching somebody else's children beside a car I couldn't drive.” On Wednesday, near the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, Denise checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I lost my license and kept quiet. I contribute by watching the driver's children for the round trip.
appearance: Denise is easy to recognize by black hair twisted into a small knot and one cheek that creases before the other. Usually dressed in a soft blue checked shirt with one cuff folded back twice, Denise folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing when listening.
personality: Denise gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Denise privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To earn a place in the rota by providing childcare.
family: Bea Rial is Denise’s half-sibling. Denise is free to hang up first. Bea makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *Window seven*, Bea says, “You can see an old handprint when the sun catches that pane.”
connections: Leon Osei. Watching children gives a rider at the furthest stop enough time to reach the lift.

reactions.situation: A driver on the rota asks for petrol money
reactions.response: Denise agrees what the fuel actually cost and discusses the contribution privately.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Denise alerts the nearest occupied shop, stays outside and writes down when the smoke first appeared.

reactions.situation: If a colleague lies to save face
reactions.response: Denise offers one private chance to correct it before the next conversation.
